ai.description: This viper reaches 60–80 cm. It is bright green with a distinct white or yellow ventrolateral stripe and a reddish-brown tail. It is distinguished by a prominent postocular stripe and keeled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus mutabilis* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid yellow or white postocular stripe that extends significantly onto the neck, unlike its congeners.
ai.habitat: The Central Nicobar Pit Viper inhabits the dense tropical evergreen and littoral forests of the Central Nicobar Islands, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Central Nicobar Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for small vertebrates among the dense foliage of its island habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus mutabilis* is viviparous, giving birth to live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with litters usually ranging from 5 to 12 neonates.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus mutabilis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring primarily within the lowland tropical forests of the Central Nicobar group.
